A 2-tap Least Mean Squares (LMS) Adaptive Filter. Automatically learns to predict a target signal d from an input x by updating filter weights w1 and w2.

Sampling Time Note: For stable learning, the sampling time (dt) must satisfy dt < 2 / (R * lr) where R is the input signal power. In practice, a sampling rate of 100 Hz to 1 kHz (dt = 1ms to 10ms) is recommended to ensure smooth gradients and prevent divergence.

xbridges.description:
A Single-Neuron Online Gradient Descent Learner using a tanh activation function. Trains weights and bias via online backpropagation.

Sampling Time Note: A sampling time of 2ms to 20ms is recommended. Smaller dt values provide smoother optimization trajectories, whereas larger dt values might cause weight divergence or numerical overflow in discrete gradient steps unless the learning rate is scaled down.

Sampling Time Note: Reinforcement learning control loops require a slower sampling time, typically 20ms to 100ms. If dt is too small, state changes are negligible, causing poor credit assignment. If dt is too large, the delayed control inputs lead to poor regulation stability.

vlab.name: Resistor
vlab.description: Linear resistor obeying Ohm's law relating terminal voltage drop to electric current.
vlab.equation: v = i * R   [V = A·Ω], v = v_p − v_n, i: p → n

vlab.name: Variable Resistor
vlab.description: A resistor whose value is controlled by an external physical signal. Useful for modeling sensors or variable loads.
vlab.equation: v = i * max(R(t), R_min)   [V = A·Ω], R(t) = signal r [Ω]

vlab.name: Infinite Resistance
vlab.description: Models an ideal open branch with zero electrical conductance (infinite resistance).

vlab.name: Capacitor
vlab.description: Electrostatic charge storage element with through current proportional to voltage derivative.
vlab.equation: i = C * dv/dt   [A = F·V/s], v(0) = v0

vlab.name: Inductor
vlab.description: Magnetic energy storage inductor with branch voltage proportional to current rate of change.
vlab.equation: v = L * di/dt   [V = H·A/s], i(0) = i0

vlab.name: Memristor
vlab.description: Two-terminal non-volatile memory resistor whose resistance varies with past charge flow.
vlab.equation:
v = M(w) * i   [V], M = M0 + 10·w [Ω]
dw/dt = i   [A]

vlab.name: Gyrator
vlab.description: Ideal non-reciprocal two-port network that inverts voltage and current characteristics.
vlab.equation:
i1 = g * v2   [A = S·V]
i2 = -g * v1   [A = S·V]

vlab.name: Ideal Transformer
vlab.description: An ideal transformer that scales voltage and current according to the turns ratio N. It preserves power (V1*I1 = V2*I2).

vlab.name: Op-Amp
vlab.description: High-gain differential operational amplifier with negative feedback virtual short behavior.
vlab.equation:
Vout = clamp(A * (V+ − V−), ±Vsat)   [V]
(linear region: V+ ≈ V− for large A)

vlab.name: Switch
vlab.description: An ideal switch controlled by a physical signal (Simscape Foundation Switch). When the control signal v exceeds threshold [V], the switch is closed with low resistance Ron [Ω]; otherwise it opens with high resistance Roff = 1/Gopen [Ω].
vlab.equation:
V = I * R_sw   [V]
R_sw = (v > threshold) ? Ron : Roff   [Ω]

vlab.name: Diode
vlab.description: Piecewise-linear diode (Simscape Electrical Diode, piecewise linear model): forward voltage Vf [V], on resistance Ron [Ω], off resistance Roff = 1/Goff [Ω]. V = v_A − v_K, current positive A → K; I(V) is continuous at V = Vf.
vlab.equation:
On (V > Vf): I = (V − Vf)/Ron + Vf/Roff   [A]
Off (V ≤ Vf): I = V/Roff   [A]

vlab.name: N-MOSFET
vlab.description: N-channel MOSFET, Shichman–Hodges (SPICE level 1) model with a physical signal gate input (gate current 0). kn = μCox·W/L [A/V²], λ [1/V]. Symmetric: drain and source swap roles for Vds < 0.
vlab.equation:
Vov = Vgs − Vth   [V]
Cut-off (Vov ≤ 0): Id = 0
Linear (0 < Vds < Vov): Id = kn·(Vov·Vds − Vds²/2)·(1 + λ·Vds)   [A]
Saturation (Vds ≥ Vov > 0): Id = kn/2·Vov²·(1 + λ·Vds)   [A]

vlab.name: IGBT
vlab.description: Ideal switching IGBT (Simscape Electrical IGBT, Ideal Switching): voltage-controlled switch with gate threshold Vge_th [V], saturation voltage Vce_sat [V], on resistance Rd [Ω] and off resistance Roff [Ω]. Conducts C → E only.
vlab.equation:
On (Vge ≥ Vge_th and Vce ≥ Vce_sat): Ic = (Vce − Vce_sat)/Rd + Vce_sat/Roff   [A]
Otherwise: Ic = Vce/Roff   [A]

vlab.name: Rotational EM Converter
vlab.description: Ideal rotational electromechanical converter (DC machine without armature inductance) between the Electrical port pair + / − and the Rotational port pair R / C. K (V·s/rad) is the back-EMF constant and, in SI, equal to the torque constant. The armature resistance R is the only loss: the electrical input V·I equals R·I² plus the mechanical power K·I·ω, so with R = 0 the conversion is lossless. K may be negative (reversed polarity).
vlab.equation:
V = R·I + K·ω [V],  ω = ω_R − ω_C [rad/s]
τ = K·I [N·m]  (torque delivered at R, reaction at C)
V·I = R·I² + τ·ω

vlab.name: Translational EM Converter
vlab.description: Ideal translational electromechanical converter (voice coil / Lorentz actuator without coil inductance) between the Electrical port pair + / − and the Translational port pair R / C. Bl (N/A = V·s/m) is the force constant and equals the back-EMF constant. The winding resistance R is the only loss: V·I = R·I² + Bl·I·v, so with R = 0 the conversion is lossless. Bl may be negative (reversed polarity).
vlab.equation:
V = R·I + Bl·v [V],  v = v_R − v_C [m/s]
F = Bl·I [N]  (force delivered at R, reaction at C)
V·I = R·I² + F·v

vlab.name: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
vlab.description: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor in the rotor-fixed dq frame (amplitude-invariant Clarke/Park transform, d axis on phase a at θ = 0). The stator terminals are the composite three-phase port ABC (wire it to an inverter / source ABC port, or through a Phase Splitter to scalar phases). Wye stator: the phase currents flow from A, B, C through the windings to the star point N, so an open N forces i_a + i_b + i_c = 0 and a connected N carries the zero-sequence current (inductance L0). The shaft is the scalar Rotational port R (speed relative to the inertial frame, the machine case is fixed to it); the torque delivered at R is τ_e − J·dω/dt − B·ω. Phase back-EMF amplitude is λm·ω_e.
vlab.equation:
v_d = Rs·i_d + Ld·di_d/dt − ω_e·Lq·i_q [V]
v_q = Rs·i_q + Lq·di_q/dt + ω_e·(Ld·i_d + λm) [V]
v_0 = Rs·i_0 + L0·di_0/dt [V]
τ_e = (3/2)·p·(λm·i_q + (Ld − Lq)·i_d·i_q) [N·m],  ω_e = p·ω [rad/s]
J·dω/dt = τ_e − B·ω − τ_shaft [N·m]

vlab.name: DC Motor
vlab.description: Permanent-magnet DC motor (Simscape DC Motor): armature circuit (Ra, La) and one electromechanical constant k [V·s/rad = N·m/A] coupled to a rotor with inertia J and viscous damping B. In SI the torque constant equals the back-EMF constant, so the conversion is lossless apart from Ra·I² and B·ω²: there is a single constant (parameter Ke). A saved model with a different Kt keeps its Ke as k and gets a migration notice. The rotor shaft is the scalar Rotational port R (speed relative to the inertial frame, the machine case is fixed to it); the torque delivered to the load is k·I minus the rotor inertia and damping terms.
vlab.equation:
V = Ra·I + La·dI/dt + k·ω [V]
τ_e = k·I = J·dω/dt + B·ω + τ_shaft [N·m]   (τ_shaft = torque delivered to the load)
V·I = Ra·I² + d(½La·I²)/dt + B·ω² + d(½J·ω²)/dt + τ_shaft·ω

vlab.name: AC Motor
vlab.description: Three-phase squirrel-cage induction motor (Krause dq0 model in the stationary αβ frame, amplitude-invariant Clarke transform, rotor referred to the stator; same T-equivalent as Simscape Asynchronous Machine Squirrel Cage). Parameters: stator/rotor resistance Rs, Rr, leakage Lls, Llr, magnetizing Lm, pole pairs P. The stator terminals are the composite three-phase port ABC (wire it to an inverter / source ABC port, or through a Phase Splitter to scalar phases). Wye stator: the phase currents flow from A, B, C through the windings to the star point N (an open N forces i_a + i_b + i_c = 0). The shaft is the scalar Rotational port R (speed relative to the inertial frame, the machine case is fixed to it).
vlab.equation:
v_s = Rs·i_s + dψ_s/dt [V]
0 = Rr·i_r + dψ_r/dt − j·P·ω·ψ_r [V]
ψ_s = (Lls + Lm)·i_s + Lm·i_r,  ψ_r = (Llr + Lm)·i_r + Lm·i_s [Wb]
τ_e = (3/2)·P·(ψ_sα·i_sβ − ψ_sβ·i_sα) [N·m]
J·dω/dt = τ_e − B·ω − τ_shaft [N·m]

vlab.name: BLDC Motor
vlab.description: Brushless DC motor with trapezoidal back-EMF (unit trapezoid f: ±1 over 120°, 60° ramps; Pillay and Krishnan, IEEE Trans. Ind. Appl. 1989). The stator terminals are the composite three-phase port ABC (wire it to an inverter / source ABC port, or through a Phase Splitter to scalar phases). Wye stator: the phase currents flow from A, B, C through the windings to the star point G (an open G forces i_a + i_b + i_c = 0). One constant Ke [V·s/rad = N·m/A] is both the back-EMF and the torque constant, so the conversion is lossless apart from Rs·i² and B·ω². Needs an external commutation bridge. The shaft is the scalar Rotational port R (speed relative to the inertial frame, the machine case is fixed to it).
vlab.equation:
v_x − v_g = Rs·i_x + Ls·di_x/dt + e_x [V],  e_x = Ke·ω·f(P·θ − φ_x),  φ = 0, 2π/3, −2π/3
τ_e = (e_a·i_a + e_b·i_b + e_c·i_c)/ω = Ke·(f_a·i_a + f_b·i_b + f_c·i_c) [N·m]
J·dω/dt = τ_e − B·ω − τ_shaft [N·m]

vlab.name: Thermal Resistor
vlab.description: Temperature-dependent electrical resistor dissipating Joule heating into the thermal domain.
vlab.equation:
V = I * R
Q_gen = I² * R

vlab.name: Scope
vlab.description: Time-domain visual scope sink displaying dynamic simulated variables across simulation time.

vlab.name: Voltage Sensor
vlab.description: Measures the potential difference between two electrical nodes and outputs it as a physical signal.
vlab.equation: V_out = V_p − V_n   [V]  (i_leak = V/R_int, R_int → ∞ ideal)

vlab.name: Current Sensor
vlab.description: Measures through electric current with zero insertion impedance and outputs a physical signal.
vlab.equation:
I_out = i_p→n   [A]
V_p − V_n = R_int * i  (R_int = 0 ideal)

vlab.name: DC Voltage Source
vlab.description: Constant DC voltage source with series internal source resistance.
vlab.equation: V_p − V_n = V + I * R_int   [V]  (I: p → n, R_int = 0 ideal)

vlab.name: AC Voltage Source
vlab.description: Sinusoidal AC voltage source generating harmonic electrical potential.
vlab.equation: V(t) = Vpk * sin(2*π*f*t + phase); Vp - Vn = V(t) + I * R_int

vlab.name: 3-Phase Source
vlab.description: Balanced wye three-phase voltage source (Simscape Three-Phase Source): V_LL = phase-to-phase RMS voltage, frequency f, phase angle φ of phase A (default 0 deg), positive a-b-c sequence. The composite port abc carries the three phase terminals (connect a Phase Splitter for the scalar phases) and the star point N is a real terminal: reference it with an Electrical Reference block. A balanced load returns zero current in N.
vlab.equation:
v_a = √(2/3)·V_LL·sin(2π·f·t + φ)
v_b = √(2/3)·V_LL·sin(2π·f·t + φ − 2π/3)
v_c = √(2/3)·V_LL·sin(2π·f·t + φ + 2π/3)   [V], phase to neutral n
i_n = −(i_a + i_b + i_c)   [A]

vlab.name: Controlled Voltage Source
vlab.description: Voltage source whose output terminal potential is commanded by a physical signal s(t).

vlab.name: DC Current Source
vlab.description: Ideal DC current source delivering constant through current independent of voltage.

vlab.name: Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source
vlab.description: Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source producing an output voltage proportional to control voltage.

vlab.name: Voltage-Controlled Current Source
vlab.description: Voltage-Controlled Current Source producing an output current proportional to control voltage.
vlab.equation: I (p → n) = Gm * (V_cp − V_cn)   [A = S·V], i_ctrl = 0

vlab.name: Current-Controlled Current Source
vlab.description: Current-Controlled Current Source producing an output current proportional to input current.
vlab.equation:
I_out (p → n) = Gain * I_ctrl   [A]
V_cp − V_cn = R_in * I_ctrl

vlab.name: Current-Controlled Voltage Source
vlab.description: Current-Controlled Voltage Source producing an output voltage proportional to input current.
vlab.equation:
V_p − V_n = Rm * I_ctrl + R_out * I_out   [V = Ω·A]
V_cp − V_cn = R_in * I_ctrl

vlab.name: Electrical Reference
vlab.description: The zero-potential reference for the electrical circuit. All voltage measurements are relative to this node.

vlab.name: Busbar
vlab.description: Ideal electrical distribution busbar maintaining equipotential connection across all attached nodes.

vlab.name: Phase Splitter
vlab.description: Splits the composite three-phase port abc into its scalar phase ports a, b and c (Simscape Phase Splitter). The phases are independent: each phase k of abc is tied to scalar port k only.
vlab.equation:
V_a = V_abc[a], V_b = V_abc[b], V_c = V_abc[c]
KCL per phase: I_abc,k = I_k

vlab.name: Delta Reference
vlab.description: Reference node for balanced delta-connected electrical topologies.
vlab.equation: V_a = 0 V   (reference node of the delta network)

vlab.name: Open Circuit
vlab.description: Maintains open-circuit condition with zero current flow at the connected port.

vlab.name: PS Three-Element Demux
vlab.description: Demultiplexes a 3-element physical signal vector into three individual scalar signals.

vlab.name: Absolute Reference (G)
vlab.description: Absolute reference node for gas networks representing standard ambient atmospheric conditions.

vlab.name: Cap (G)
vlab.description: Hermetic pneumatic end cap blocking gas mass flow at a conduit termination.

vlab.name: Rotational Mechanical Converter (G)
vlab.description: Ideal positive-displacement rotary machine (vane or piston motor / compressor) between the gas ports A and H and the Rotational ports R / C. D (m³/rad) is the displacement: the volumetric flow at A is D·ω and the shaft torque is D·(P_A − P_H), so the shaft power τ·ω equals the pressure power (P_A − P_H)·V̇ and no power is lost. The gas is ideal at the fixed temperature T (R_gas = 287 J/(kg·K), air). Positive ω pumps gas from A to H.
vlab.equation:
ṁ(A→H) = ρ_A·D·ω [kg/s],  ρ_A = P_A/(R_gas·T),  ω = ω_R − ω_C [rad/s]
τ = D·(P_A − P_H) [N·m]  (torque delivered at R, reaction at C)
(P_A − P_H)·ṁ/ρ_A = −τ_in·ω

vlab.name: Translational Mechanical Converter (G)
vlab.description: Ideal double-acting pneumatic cylinder between the gas ports A and H and the Translational ports R / C. A (m²) is the piston area: the volumetric flow at A is A·v and the piston force is A·(P_A − P_H), so the mechanical power F·v equals the pressure power (P_A − P_H)·V̇ and no power is lost. The gas is ideal at the fixed temperature T (R_gas = 287 J/(kg·K), air). Positive v pumps gas from A to H.
vlab.equation:
ṁ(A→H) = ρ_A·A·v [kg/s],  ρ_A = P_A/(R_gas·T),  v = v_R − v_C [m/s]
F = A·(P_A − P_H) [N]  (force delivered at R, reaction at C)
(P_A − P_H)·ṁ/ρ_A = −F_in·v

vlab.name: Gear Box
vlab.description: Ideal (lossless, massless, backlash-free) simple gear between shaft S1 (input / follower side, faster) and shaft S2 (output / base side); both shafts are scalar Rotational ports referenced to the inertial frame. ratio = ω1/ω2 (dimensionless, nonzero; a ratio of 0 is rejected). A positive ratio makes both shafts rotate in the same direction and a negative ratio reverses the direction (the Simscape Simple Gear 'output shaft rotates in the opposite direction' setting); the magnitude is the teeth ratio. The torque delivered to S2 is the torque into S1 multiplied by the ratio, so the transmitted power is zero for either sign.
vlab.equation:
ω1 = ratio·ω2 [rad/s]
τ1,in·ratio + τ2,in = 0 [N·m]   (delivered τ2 = ratio·τ1; P = τ1·ω1 + τ2·ω2 = 0)

vlab.name: Lever
vlab.description: Ideal massless rigid lever pivoting about port C, with port A at arm length L1 on one side of the pivot and port B at arm length L2 on the opposite side (small-angle, translational ports). Port C is the pivot (fulcrum) and carries the reaction force F_C = −(F_A + F_B); the pivot may move (v_C) or be tied to a Translational reference. A positive velocity at A gives a negative velocity at B relative to the pivot, with v_A/v_B = −L1/L2; the moment balance about the pivot is F_A·L1 = F_B·L2. Lossless: the three port powers sum to zero.
vlab.equation:
(v_A − v_C)·L2 + (v_B − v_C)·L1 = 0 [m/s·m]   (opposite sides of the pivot: v_A − v_C = −(L1/L2)·(v_B − v_C))
F_A·L1 − F_B·L2 = 0,  F_A + F_B + F_C = 0 [N]   (forces into the block; P = F_A·v_A + F_B·v_B + F_C·v_C = 0)

vlab.name: Wheel and Axle
vlab.description: Ideal wheel and axle (rolling without slip, lossless): the Translational port P moves at v = Rw·ω of the Rotational axle A (both referenced to the inertial frame) and the axle torque is the wheel radius times the force, τ = Rw·F, so the transmitted power is zero. Rw > 0 (m).
vlab.equation:
v_P = Rw·ω_A [m/s]
τ_A,in + Rw·F_P,in = 0 [N·m]   (P = τ_A·ω_A + F_P·v_P = 0)

vlab.name: Rotational Multibody Interface
vlab.description: Scalar-to-Frame bridge for a Rotational network (one of the only two allowed scalar/Frame connections). Wire B and F in parallel with the Frames of a joint (for example a Revolute Joint) that has the same axis: the angular velocity of F relative to B about the normalized B-local axis parameter is imposed on the Rotational port pair R-C (ω_R − ω_C = ω_rel), and the torque T of the Rotational network is applied as a pure couple T·a on F with the reaction −T·a on B, about the configured axis (never a fixed X or Z axis). Ideal and lossless: T·ω_rel is handed from the network to the Frames. Output w is ω_rel (rad/s).
vlab.equation:
ω_R − ω_C = ω_rel = a·(ω_F − ω_B)  [rad/s],  a = R_B·axis (world)
τ_F = T·a,  τ_B = −T·a  [N·m]   (T = torque from R to C; P = T·ω_rel)

vlab.name: Translational Multibody Interface
vlab.description: Scalar-to-Frame bridge for a Translational network (one of the only two allowed scalar/Frame connections). Wire B and F in parallel with the Frames of a joint (for example a Prismatic Joint) that has the same axis: the slide rate of F relative to B along the normalized B-local axis parameter is imposed on the Translational port pair R-C (v_R − v_C = v_rel), and the force F of the Translational network is applied along that axis on F with the reaction on B (including the moment of the lever arm P_F − P_B), never along a fixed X axis. Ideal and lossless: F·v_rel is handed from the network to the Frames. Output v is v_rel (m/s).
vlab.equation:
v_R − v_C = v_rel = d/dt (a·(P_F − P_B))  [m/s],  a = R_B·axis (world)
f_F = F·a,  f_B = −F·a,  τ_B = −(P_F − P_B) × F·a   (F = force from R to C; P = F·v_rel)

vlab.name: 3-Phase Inverter Bridge
vlab.description: Two-level three-phase voltage-source inverter. Model mode 'averaged' (default) is the Simscape Average-Value Inverter: continuous duty d_k, no switching ripple. Model mode 'switching' is the ideal-switch model: each leg switches at f_sw when the duty reference crosses a triangular carrier (anti-parallel diodes, no dead time), and the crossing instants are located by the solver's zero-crossing events. AC terminals are the composite three-phase port ABC (connect it to a machine ABC port directly, or through a Phase Splitter to scalar phases); DC+ / DC− are the DC link. References: input vabc = (m_a, m_b, m_c) in [−1, 1] (control mode three_phase_modulation; legacy scalar duties d_a, d_b, d_c in [0, 1] when vabc is unwired, an unwired duty means the lower switch is on), or, in control mode sinusoidal_modulation, an internal balanced V/f generator at the output frequency with amplitude M (input M, or the Modulation Index parameter). Linear range M ≤ 1: line-to-line fundamental rms = (√3/(2√2))·M·Vdc; over-modulation saturates at the rails. The AC side is a voltage source behind R_out, so a floating (wye, open star point) load sees no zero-sequence current.
vlab.equation:
v_k − v_n = d_k·Vdc − R_out·i_k,out  [V],  k = a, b, c  (Vdc = v_DC+ − v_DC−)
i_dc = Σ d_k·i_k,out  [A]  (P_dc = Σ v_k·i_k,out + R_out·Σ i_k,out²)
d_k = (1 + m_k)/2,  m_k = M·sin(2π·f_out·t − k·2π/3)  or the vabc / duty inputs  → fundamental pole amplitude = M·Vdc/2

vlab.name: PWM Generator (3-Phase, 3-Level)
vlab.description: Three-level (neutral-point-clamped) phase-disposition PWM generator (Simscape PWM Generator (Three-Level)). Input m_abc = (m_a, m_b, m_c) is the reference vector in [−1, 1] (unit = Vdc/2); two in-phase triangular carriers at f_sw (upper in [0, 1], lower in [−1, 0]) turn it into the level commands ga, gb, gc ∈ {−1, 0, +1} (+Vdc/2 / neutral / −Vdc/2 at the phase output of an NPC leg); ma, mb, mc echo the clamped references. The carrier average of the level equals the reference for every |m| ≤ 1, so the fundamental phase voltage is m·Vdc/2 and the line-to-line rms fundamental (√3/(2√2))·m·Vdc. vdc and vneut (DC-link total and neutral-point unbalance) add a bounded zero-sequence offset Δ_neut that steers the neutral point. This is a signal generator (it computes gate levels, not a power stage): connect the levels to switch / IGBT commands of an NPC leg.
vlab.equation:
r_k = clamp(m_k + Δ_neut, −1, 1),  Δ_neut = clamp(k_neut·v_neut/max(|v_dc|, 1), −0.15, 0.15)
c_u = tri(f_sw·t) ∈ [0, 1],  c_l = c_u − 1
g_k = +1 if r_k ≥ c_u,  −1 if r_k ≤ c_l,  0 otherwise  → v_k = g_k·Vdc/2 ∈ {−Vdc/2, 0, +Vdc/2}
⟨g_k⟩ over a carrier period = r_k  (fundamental phase voltage = m·Vdc/2)

vlab.name: PWM Generator (Vienna Rectifier)
vlab.description: Carrier-based PWM generator of a three-phase three-level Vienna rectifier (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-vienna-rectifier-pwm-design.md). The phase-switch duty is 1 − |m_x|, so with the diode legs the average pole voltage is sign(i_x)·|m_x|·Vdc/2 = v_x at unity power factor (m_x = 2·v_x/Vdc is the feed-forward term). An outer proportional DC-link loop (kp_v, vdc_ref) scales the in-phase current reference I*, a fixed 0.05 V/A current-error gain corrects the modulation, and vneut adds a bounded zero-sequence term that balances the neutral point. Outputs ga, gb, gc ∈ {0, 1} are the switch gates, ma, mb, mc the modulation indices. Signal generator only (no power stage): wire the gates to the bidirectional phase switches of a Vienna bridge built from diodes and IGBT / switch blocks. The scalar ports are kept as in the spec (one phase per port).
vlab.equation:
I* = max(0, kp_v·(vdc_ref − vdc))  [A]
Δ_neut = clamp(k_neut·v_neut/max(|vdc|, 1), −0.2, 0.2)
m_x = clamp(2·v_x/max(|vdc|, 1) + 0.05·(I*·v_x/max(√(v_a²+v_b²+v_c²), 1) − i_x) + Δ_neut, −1, 1)
g_x = 1 if C_tri(f_sw·t) < 1 − |m_x| else 0   (switch on = phase clamped to the neutral)

vlab.name: Thyristor 6-Pulse Generator
vlab.description: Six-pulse firing generator for a thyristor (Graetz) bridge (Simscape Synchronized 6-Pulse Generator). Gate k = 1…6 is high for pulse_width degrees starting at the firing angle α + 60·(k − 1), α counted from the natural commutation point of thyristor 1 (with v_a = V·sin ωt and positive a-b-c sequence that is θ = ωt − 30°). θ is the synchronisation angle in degrees (absolute); unwired, the block uses its own ramp 360·freq·t. A six-pulse bridge with firing angle α has the mean DC voltage (3√2/π)·V_LL·cos α. Signal generator only; the library has no thyristor device, so the gates drive controlled switches.
vlab.equation:
g_k = 1 if wrap360(θ − (α + 60·(k − 1))) < pulse_width,  else 0   [θ, α in deg],  k = 1…6
θ = 360·freq·t when the θ port is unwired
Diode / thyristor bridge: Vdc,avg = (3√2/π)·V_LL·cos α  (ripple at 6·f)

vlab.name: Thyristor 12-Pulse Generator
vlab.description: Twelve-pulse firing generator (Simscape Synchronized 12-Pulse Generator): two six-pulse sequences, the wye (star) bridge 30° behind the delta bridge, each gate 60° after the previous one. θ is a phase offset in radians that is added to the internal ramp 2π·freq·t (the six-pulse block takes an absolute angle in degrees instead), α is the firing angle in degrees. Two six-pulse bridges fed 30° apart and connected in series give twice the six-pulse mean DC voltage with the ripple at 12 times the line frequency. Signal generator only; the library has no thyristor device, so the gates drive controlled switches.
vlab.equation:
φ = θ + 2π·freq·t  [rad]
delta_g_k = 1 if wrap2π(φ − (α + 60·(k − 1))) < pulse_width,  else 0
wye_g_k = 1 if wrap2π(φ − (α + 30 + 60·(k − 1))) < pulse_width,  else 0   [α, pulse_width in deg],  k = 1…6
12-pulse bridge pair in series: Vdc,avg = 2·(3√2/π)·V_LL·cos α  (ripple at 12·f)

vlab.name: Belt-Cable Properties
vlab.description: Property link: publishes the linear density ρ (kg/m) and the Young modulus E (Pa) to every Belt-Cable End, Spool and Pulley wired to its BeltProperty port P. It has no mechanical ports and exchanges no power; a belt block that is not wired to it uses its own stiffness / inertia parameters.
vlab.equation:
ρ = linear density [kg/m],  E = Young modulus [Pa]
k = E·A/L [N/m] (Belt-Cable End),  J_belt = 2π·ρ·R³ [kg·m²] (spool, pulley)

vlab.name: Belt-Cable End
vlab.description: Elastic (tension-carrying) end of a belt or cable between two Translational ports R and E, k = E·A/L from a wired Belt-Cable Properties block (Young modulus E, section A, length L), otherwise the stiffness parameter. The stored energy is ½·k·x² and no power is dissipated (no internal damping parameter is exposed). Output f is the belt tension, positive when the belt is stretched (E moves away from R).
vlab.equation:
dx/dt = v_R − v_E [m/s]
F_R→E = k·x [N],  k = E·A/L (linked Belt-Cable Properties) or stiffness [N/m]
f = −F_R→E = k·(x_E − x_R)  (belt tension, N)

vlab.name: Belt-Cable Spool
vlab.description: Ideal spool (winch) that reels a belt or cable: the belt end at Translational port A moves at v = R·ω of the Rotational shaft R (both referenced to the inertial frame). The torque balance includes the spool inertia plus the inertia of one wrapped circumference of belt, ρ·2π·R·R², with ρ the linear density of a wired Belt-Cable Properties block. Power balance: τ·ω + F·v = d(½·J·ω²)/dt. Output t is the torque the shaft delivers into the spool (N·m).
vlab.equation:
v_A = R·ω_R [m/s]
τ_R,in + R·F_A,in = J·dω/dt [N·m],  J = inertia + 2π·ρ·R³ (wrapped belt)
t = τ_R,in

vlab.name: Pulley
vlab.description: Ideal pulley carrying a belt over a wheel of radius R: the two belt segments A and B (Translational ports) move in opposite directions at ±R·ω of the Rotational hub R. The torque balance includes the hub inertia plus the wrapped-belt inertia 2π·ρ·R³ (linear density ρ from a wired Belt-Cable Properties block). Power balance: τ·ω + F_A·v_A + F_B·v_B = d(½·J·ω²)/dt. Output t is the torque the hub delivers into the pulley (N·m).
vlab.equation:
v_A = R·ω [m/s],  v_B = −R·ω [m/s]
τ_R,in + R·(F_A,in − F_B,in) = J·dω/dt [N·m],  J = inertia + 2π·ρ·R³
t = τ_R,in

vlab.name: Revolute Joint
vlab.description: 1-DOF revolute joint: rotation about the normalized B-local axis a (a is also the F-local axis at q = 0). Constrains the 3 relative translations and the 2 rotations perpendicular to a. Reactions are the Lagrange multipliers of those 5 constraints: force Ff on F (equal and opposite on B) and the constrained torque, always perpendicular to a. Damping c [N*m*s/rad] acts only on the free rotation about a (0 is allowed). Outputs: q [rad] and w [rad/s] about the axis, reaction force (fx, fy, fz, f_reac) and torque (tx, ty, tz total on F including damping; t_reac is the constrained part only).
vlab.equation: Pf = Pb; (Rb t_j) . (Rf a) = 0 for t_j perpendicular to a (j = 1, 2); Ff = -Fb; Tf = sum_j lambda_j ((Rf a) x (Rb t_j)) - c w (Rb a); Tb = -Tf

vlab.name: Prismatic Joint
vlab.description: 1-DOF prismatic joint: translation along the normalized B-local axis a. Constrains the 2 translations perpendicular to a and all 3 rotations. Reactions are the Lagrange multipliers of those 5 constraints: constraint force perpendicular to a (f_reac) plus the viscous force c v along a (fx, fy, fz are the total force on F), and the 3 constrained torques (tx, ty, tz on F about F; tbx, tby, tbz on B about B, which include the lever arm of the displacement). Damping c [N*s/m] acts only on the slide (0 is allowed). Outputs: displacement x [m] and velocity v [m/s].
vlab.equation: (Rb c_j) . (Pf - Pb) = 0 for c_j perpendicular to a (j = 1, 2); Rf = Rb; Ff = sum_j lambda_j (Rb c_j) - c v (Rb a); Tb = -Tf - (Pf - Pb) x Ff

vlab.name: Spherical Joint
vlab.description: Ideal 3-DOF ball-and-socket joint: locks the relative X/Y/Z translation and leaves every rotation free, so it transmits no torque (there is no rotational damping or friction model). Reactions are the 3 force multipliers (fx, fy, fz, f_reac) in N. Outputs rx, ry, rz are the relative rotation vector (angle times axis of Rb^T Rf) in rad.
vlab.equation: Pf - Pb = 0; Ff = -Fb (3 multipliers); Tf = Tb = 0

vlab.name: Universal Joint
vlab.description: Two-axis universal joint. axis1 belongs to B and axis2 to F; nonparallel reference axes are orthonormalized. Angles are signed principal values in rad; t_reac is signed constrained torque on F. Damping opposes permitted-axis angular velocity only.
vlab.equation: Pf = Pb; (Rb axis1) dot (Rf axis2) = 0; equal/opposite reactions

vlab.name: Weld Joint
vlab.description: 0-DOF weld: locks all 6 relative coordinates to the fixed reference pose given by offset p0 (B-local, m) and rotation R0 (deg, Z-Y-X Euler like Rigid Transform); the default is coincident, aligned frames. Reactions are the 6 multipliers: force fx, fy, fz and torque tx, ty, tz exerted on F, plus the torque on B about B (tbx, tby, tbz = -t - d x f, which carries the moment of an offset load). pos_err [m] and rot_err [rad] report the residual relative pose error. There is no stiffness: the constraint is ideal.
vlab.equation: Pf - Pb - Rb p0 = 0; Rf = Rb R0; Ff = -Fb; Tb = -Tf - (Pf - Pb) x Ff (6 multipliers)

vlab.name: Common Gear Constraint
vlab.description: Ideal (lossless, massless, backlash-free) gear pair between two scalar Rotational shafts B (base) and F (follower), each referenced to the inertial frame. ratio = ω_F/ω_B (dimensionless, nonzero); a negative ratio is an external mesh that reverses the direction. The constraint forces τ_F = -τ_B/ratio on the follower, so the transmitted power is zero. Both ports are scalar Rotational ports (the Simscape Driveline style): attach a body through a Rotational Multibody Interface, never wire a Frame to this block.
vlab.equation:
ω_F = ratio·ω_B [rad/s]
τ_B,in + ratio·τ_F,in = 0 [N·m]  (P = τ_B·ω_B + τ_F·ω_F = 0)

vlab.name: Rack and Pinion Constraint
vlab.description: Ideal rack and pinion between a scalar Rotational pinion shaft B and a scalar Translational rack F, both referenced to the inertial frame. Positive pinion rotation drives the rack in the positive direction (v = r·ω); the rack force reacts on the pinion as τ = r·F, so the transmitted power is zero. Pinion pitch radius r > 0 (m). Scalar Rotational/Translational ports (Simscape Driveline style); a Frame must be attached through a Multibody Interface block.
vlab.equation:
v_F = r·ω_B [m/s]
τ_B,in + r·F_F,in = 0 [N·m]  (P = τ_B·ω_B + F_F·v_F = 0)

vlab.name: Mechanism Configuration

It contributes no wrench and no constraint equation. Gravity is applied by the Gravitational Field block (this block records the mechanism gravity and rejects a malformed vector).
